readings.title: Jacob’s Wages
readings.subtitle: The Strengthening of Jacob’s Flocks
readings.text: [Genesis 30:25] And it came to be, when Raḥel had borne <dn>את</dn> Yosěph, that Ya‛aqoḇ said to Laḇan, “Send me away, that I may go to my own place and to my land. [26] “Give me <dn>את</dn> my wives and <dn>את</dn> my children for whom I have served you, and let me go, for you know <dn>את</dn> my service which I have done for you.” [27] And Laḇan said to him, “If I have found favour in your eyes, please stay, for I have observed that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed me for your sake.” [28] And he said, “Name me your wages, and I give it.” [29] And he said to him, “You know <dn>את</dn> how I have served you and <dn>את</dn> how your livestock has been with me. [30] “For the little you had before I came has increased to a great amount, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed you since my coming. And now, when am I to provide for my own house too?” [31] And he said, “What do I give you?” And Ya‛aqoḇ said, “Give me nothing. If you do this for me, I shall again feed and guard your flocks: [32] “Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from there all the speckled and spotted sheep, and all the black sheep among the lambs, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. And these shall be my wages. [33] “And my righteousness shall answer for me in time to come, when you come concerning my wages: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the lambs, it is stolen if it is with me.” [34] And Laḇan said, “See, let it be according to your word.” [35] And on that day he removed <dn>את</dn> the he-goats that were speckled and spotted, and <dn>את</dn> all the she-goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had some white in it, and <dn>את</dn> all the black ones among the lambs, and gave them into the hand of his sons. [36] And he put three days’ journey between himself and Ya‛aqoḇ, and Ya‛aqoḇ fed <dn>את</dn> the rest of Laḇan’s flocks. [37] And Ya‛aqoḇ took for himself rods of green poplar and of the almond and chestnut trees, peeled white strips in them, and exposed <dn>את</dn> the white which was in the rods. [38] And <dn>את</dn> the rods which he had peeled, he set before the flocks in the gutters, in the watering troughs where the flocks came to drink, so that they should conceive when they came to drink. [39] And the flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks brought forth streaked, speckled, and spotted. [40] And Ya‛aqoḇ separated the lambs, and made the flocks face toward the streaked and all the black in the flock of Laḇan. And he put his own herds by themselves and did not put them with Laḇan’s flock. [41] And it came to be, whenever the stronger livestock conceived, that Ya‛aqoḇ placed <dn>את</dn> the rods before the eyes of the livestock in the gutters, so they would conceive among the rods. [42] But when the livestock were feeble, he did not put them in. So the feeble were Laḇan’s and the stronger Ya‛aqoḇ’s. [43] And the man increased exceedingly, and had many flocks, and female servants and male servants, and camels and donkeys.

readings.title: Jacob Flees Laban
readings.subtitle: The Command to Return to Canaan
readings.text: [Genesis 31:1] And he heard <dn>את</dn> the words of Laḇan’s sons, saying, “Ya‛aqoḇ has taken away <dn>את</dn> all that was our father’s, and from what was our father’s he has acquired <dn>את</dn> all this esteem.” [2] And Ya‛aqoḇ saw <dn>את</dn> the face of Laḇan, and see, it was not toward him as before. [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Ya‛aqoḇ, <dq>“Return to the land of your fathers and to your relatives. And <dn>I</dn> am with you.”</dq> [4] And Ya‛aqoḇ sent and called Raḥel and Lě’ah to the field, to his flock, [5] and said to them, “I see <dn>את</dn> your father’s face, that it is not toward me as before. But the <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father has been with me. [6] “And you know that I have served <dn>את</dn> your father with all my strength. [7] “Yet your father has deceived me and changed <dn>את</dn> my wages ten times, but <dn>Elohim</dn> did not allow him to do evil to me. [8] “If he said this, ‘The speckled are your wages,’ then all the flocks bore speckled. And if he said this, ‘The streaked are your wages,’ then all the flocks bore streaked. [9] “So <dn>Elohim</dn> has taken away <dn>את</dn> the livestock of your father and given them to me. [10] “And it came to be, at the time the livestock conceived, that I lifted my eyes and looked in a dream, and see, the rams which leaped upon the flocks were streaked, speckled, and mottled. [11] “And <dn>The Messenger of Elohim</dn> spoke to me in a dream, ‘Ya‛aqoḇ.’ And I said, ‘Here I am.’ [12] “And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>‘Lift your eyes now and see, all the rams which leap on the flocks are streaked, speckled, and mottled, for <dn>I</dn> have seen <dn>את</dn> all that Laḇan is doing to you.</dq> [13] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am the <dn>Ěl</dn> of Běyth Ěl, where you anointed the standing column and where you made a vow to <dn>Me</dn>. Now rise up, get out of this land, and return to the land of your relatives.’ ”</dq> [14] And Raḥel and Lě’ah answered and said to him, “Is there still any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house? [15] “Are we not reckoned by him as strangers? For he has sold us, and also entirely consumed <dn>את</dn> our money. [16] “For all the riches which <dn>Elohim</dn> has taken from our father are ours and our children’s. And now, do whatever <dn>Elohim</dn> has said to you.” [17] Then Ya‛aqoḇ rose and set <dn>את</dn> his sons and <dn>את</dn> his wives on camels, [18] and he led away <dn>את</dn> all his livestock and <dn>את</dn> all his possessions which he had acquired, his purchase of livestock which he had acquired in Paddan Aram, to go to his father Yitsḥaq in the land of Kena‛an. [19] And Laḇan had gone to shear <dn>את</dn> his sheep, and Raḥel stole <dn>את</dn> the house idols that were her father’s. [20] And Ya‛aqoḇ stole <dn>את</dn> the heart of Laḇan the Aramean, because he did not inform him that he intended to flee. [21] So he fled with all that he had. And he rose up and passed over <dn>את</dn> the River, and set <dn>את</dn> his face toward the mountains of Gil‛aḏ.

readings.title: Laban Overtakes Jacob
readings.subtitle: The Search for the Idols
readings.text: [Genesis 31:22] And on the third day Laḇan was told that Ya‛aqoḇ had fled. [23] Then he took <dn>את</dn> his brothers with him and pursued him for seven days’ journey, and he overtook <dn>את</dn> him in the mountains of Gil‛aḏ. [24] And <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Laḇan the Aramean in a dream by night, and said to him, <dq>“Guard yourself, lest you speak to Ya‛aqoḇ either good or evil.”</dq> [25] And Laḇan overtook <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ. Now Ya‛aqoḇ had pitched <dn>את</dn> his tent in the mountains, and Laḇan with his brothers pitched in the mountains of Gil‛aḏ. [26] And Laḇan said to Ya‛aqoḇ, “What have you done, that you have stolen <dn>את</dn> my heart, and driven my daughters away like captives taken with the sword? [27] “Why did you flee secretly and steal away from me, and not inform me, for I would have sent you away with rejoicing and songs, with timbrel and lyre? [28] “And you did not allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters. Now you have been foolish in doing this. [29] “It is in the power of my hand to do evil to you, but the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your father spoke to me last night, saying, <dq>‘Guard yourself, lest you speak to Ya‛aqoḇ either good or evil.’</dq> [30] “And now you have gone because you greatly longed for your father’s house, but why did you steal <dn>את</dn> my mighty ones?” [31] And Ya‛aqoḇ answered and said to Laḇan, “Because I was afraid, for I said, ‘Lest you tear <dn>את</dn> your daughters away from me.’ [32] “With whomever you find <dn>את</dn> your mighty ones, do not let him live. In the presence of our brothers, see for yourself what is with me and take it with you.” For Ya‛aqoḇ did not know that Raḥel had stolen them. [33] And Laḇan went into Ya‛aqoḇ’s tent, and into Lě’ah’s tent, and into the tents of the two female servants, but he did not find them. And he came out of Lě’ah’s tent and entered Raḥel’s tent. [34] Now Raḥel had taken <dn>את</dn> the house idols and put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. And Laḇan searched <dn>את</dn> all about the tent but did not find them. [35] And she said to her father, “Let it not be displeasing in the eyes of my master that I am unable to rise before you, for the way of women is upon me.” And he searched but did not find <dn>את</dn> the house idols. [36] And Ya‛aqoḇ was wroth, and strove with Laḇan. And Ya‛aqoḇ answered and said to Laḇan, “What is my transgression? What is my sin, that you have hotly pursued me? [37] “Now that you have searched <dn>את</dn> all my goods, what have you found of all your household goods? Set it here before my brothers and your brothers, and let them decide between the two of us! [38] “These twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your female goats have not miscarried their young, and I have not eaten the rams of your flock. [39] “That which was torn by beasts I did not bring to you, I bore the loss of it. You required it from my hand, whether stolen by day or stolen by night. [40] “I was: by day the heat consumed me, and the frost by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes. [41] “These twenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed <dn>את</dn> my wages ten times. [42] “Unless the <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham and the <dn>Fear</dn> of Yitsḥaq, had been with me, you would now have sent me away empty-handed. <dn>Elohim</dn> has seen <dn>את</dn> my affliction and <dn>את</dn> the labour of my hands, and rendered judgment last night.”

readings.title: The Covenant at Mizpah
readings.subtitle: A Heap of Witness
readings.text: [Genesis 31:43] And Laḇan answered and said to Ya‛aqoḇ, “These daughters are my daughters, and these children are my children, and this flock is my flock, and all that you see is mine. But what shall I do today to these my daughters or to their children whom they have borne? [44] “And now, come, let us make a covenant, you and I, and it shall be a witness between you and me.” [45] So Ya‛aqoḇ took a stone and set it up as a standing column. [46] And Ya‛aqoḇ said to his brothers, “Gather stones.” And they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there on the heap. [47] And Laḇan called it Yeg̱ar Sahaḏutha, but Ya‛aqoḇ called it Gal‛ěḏ. [48] And Laḇan said, “This heap is a witness between you and me this day.” That is why its name was called Gal‛ěḏ, [49] also Mits-pah, because he said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> watch between you and me when we are out of each other’s sight. [50] “If you afflict <dn>את</dn> my daughters, or if you take other wives besides my daughters, although no man is with us—see, <dn>Elohim</dn> is witness between you and me!” [51] And Laḇan said to Ya‛aqoḇ, “See this heap and see this standing column which I have placed between you and me. [52] “This heap is a witness, and this standing column is a witness, that I do not pass beyond <dn>את</dn> this heap to you, and you do not pass beyond <dn>את</dn> this heap and <dn>את</dn> this standing column to me, for evil. [53] “The <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Naḥor, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of their father, judge between us.” And Ya‛aqoḇ swore by the <dn>Fear</dn> of his father Yitsḥaq. [54] And Ya‛aqoḇ slaughtered a slaughtering on the mountain, and called his brothers to eat bread. And they ate bread and spent the night on the mountain. [55] And Laḇan rose up early in the morning, and kissed his sons and daughters and blessed them. And Laḇan left and returned to his place.
